Hi Samira — great meeting today, thanks for walking us through your search/ranking workflow. Quick recap and the technical asks we agreed to follow up on: 

1) Goals we heard
- Replace current monolithic ranking pipeline with a hybrid approach: model embeddings for candidate retrieval + a lightweight reranker to rescore with structured signals and tool-calls.
- Lock down credentials and rotation so your SecOps can sign off (SOC2 gap currently).

2) Technical scope for POC
- SDK footprint: embed + rerank client in your Python service (auto-batching enabled).
- Auth choices to evaluate: short-lived OAuth/JWT issued from your IdP -> exchange to Redwood short-lived key (STS), OR scoped long-lived API keys with strict IP & route restrictions.
- Service account pattern: dedicated service account per environment (sandbox/staging/prod), with permissions limited to inference.generate, embeddings.create, rerank.execute, tools.invoke.
- Rotation: prefer automated short-lived tokens (recommended) backed by your KMS/HSM for signing; fallback plan for customers using Vault-managed API keys.

3) Security artifacts you asked for
- Scope matrix (attached)
- Proposed integration diagram (attached)
- Example token-exchange flow and sample SDK snippet (link below)

4) Next steps (proposed timeline)
- This week: Ben to send an implementation checklist and recommended IAM roles.
- By Wed: Redwood team to provision a sandbox model endpoint and demo credentials that rotate every 12 hours.
- Week of 5/24: 2-day POC where Quantify runs a small dataset for retrieval + rerank.

Questions for you (please confirm):
- Do you have a central secrets manager (Hashi Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager)?
- Any blocking compliance requirements for HSM-backed key material?

If this recap looks right I’ll convert into a mutual action plan and lock specific dates. Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Samira — quick technical response to the questions above and the sample flow you requested. Long version below, TL;DR at top.

TL;DR
- We support BYOK for KMS/HSM: Redwood Private can accept customer-managed keys for signing short-lived tokens; hosted customers can use our HSM-backed signing with an attestation workflow.
- Recommended pattern: OIDC assertion (IdP) -> Redwood STS token exchange -> short-lived scoped JWT (1h) signed by Redwood trusting your public key or by Redwood HSM when BYOK unavailable.
- For reranker/tool-calls: SDK does mTLS outbound when configured; tool-calls happen on the server side with a dedicated tools.invoke scope.

Detailed notes
1) Auth patterns we propose for POC (ranked by security + operational burden)
A) Short-lived federated tokens (recommended)
- Flow: Your IdP issues short OIDC tokens for a Quantify service account -> Quantify service calls Redwood STS /token-exchange endpoint with assertion -> Redwood issues short-lived JWT scoped to inference endpoints (1 hour TTL)
- Benefits: no long-lived material on Quantify side; easy to rotate; maps to least privilege per env.
- Requirements: public key or OIDC metadata from your IdP; for HSM requirement we can sign the resulting JWT with your BYOK key or Redwood HSM based on the trust model.

B) Scoped long-lived API keys (operationally simplest but less secure)
- Use with strict IP allowlists, per-route restrictions, and rotated monthly via automation. Good fallback if IdP integration is blocked.

C) Vault-managed service-account keys (medium)
- Quantify stores service-account private keys in Vault; a short-lived token is minted by Quantify to call Redwood. Stills avoids storing raw keys in code.

2) Reranker + tool-calling considerations
- Tools.invoke scope: every tool integration must be requested explicitly; we can issue scoped tokens that exclude tool invocation for read-only ingestion services.
- mTLS: the Redwood SDK supports client certs for outbound calls and can validate your server certs. We recommend terminating mTLS at your side and using token-based auth between SDK and Redwood.
- Structured output / tool-calling: we’ll provide a model wrapper that emits a structured JSON envelope for the reranker to consume; see link in attachments for the sample schema.

3) Rotation and automation
- We’ll provide a sample Jenkins/GitHubAction job that rotates API keys and updates the Vault/Key Vault secret. For short-lived tokens, rotation is handled by the IdP -> STS flow.
- Audit logs: Redwood can stream auth events (token-issue, token-exchange, invalidated-key) to your SIEM via webhook or forwarder.

4) Sandbox provisioning
- We’ll spin up a sandbox endpoint with the following: ephemeral service-account, STS endpoint enabled, and a sample reranker pipeline. Credentials will rotate every 12 hours; we will also publish a small dataset to reproduce retrieval+rerank results.

Next steps (from Ben)
- I’ll drop a one-page STS flow diagram and sample cURL for token-exchange by EOD today.
- Marissa will follow up on provisioning timelines and provide a sandbox endpoint URL.

If you need a deeper dive on the HSM attestation / BYOK handshake I can loop in our security lead.
